summary_paragraph: A 72-year-old woman with a history of liver transplant for HCV cirrhosis, chronic kidney disease, and type 2 diabetes was admitted after being found down at home with confusion and weakness. She reported dysuria and loose stools, and evaluation revealed a Klebsiella urinary tract infection, elevated creatinine of 2.8 consistent with prerenal azotemia, and a blood glucose of 438. She experienced a nonconvulsive seizure, prompting neurology consultation and initiation of levetiracetam. Brain imaging showed no acute abnormalities, and EEG indicated mild encephalopathy likely due to the infection. She was treated with aztreonam for three days, but a repeat urine culture showed contamination, so antibiotics were discontinued. Her mental status improved, kidney function stabilized, and blood sugar was controlled with increased insulin. She was discharged home with services on levetiracetam, adjusted tacrolimus and insulin, and plans for outpatient follow-up.
